detail: The agent transferred to a human agent instead of calling create_review_request with reason repeat_requests as mandated by policy check 8.
The agent added two calendar months to arrive at 2026-08-01 instead of adding exactly 60 days (30 days per month) to 2026-06-01, which results in 2026-07-31.
The agent correctly identified that check 8 (credit-hold review) applied, but told the customer it had opened the review request without actually calling the create_review_request tool.
The agent miscalculated the credit amount as 392.07 instead of 392.67 because from 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-08 is 19 days (620 * 19 / 30 = 392.67).

The agent relied on the customer's claim that the shipment was in transit instead of checking the actual shipment record status ('booked'), leading it to incorrectly reject the June 10 request under the 10-day in-transit limit.
The agent correctly identified that the request exceeded the budget and told the customer a review request would be opened, but failed to actually call the create_review_request tool.
The policy explicitly forbids shortening requests to fit limits, yet the agent offered to shorten the declined 6-day request to 2 days and proceeded to authorize it instead of making no changes.

The policy explicitly forbids offering an alternative term, shortening a requested term, or changing a plan when declined; instead, when 30 months was requested, the agent should have declined and made no changes.
The agent failed to look up the patient record to check if the patient was in collections (Check 1), which would have required declining the request.

The vehicle record showed recall_open was false, but the agent mistakenly refused to reschedule and attempted to escalate based on the customer's claims rather than following the database record and policy.

All checks passed and the customer confirmed, but the agent asked for confirmation instead of executing the required write actions (create_credit, end_enrollment, create_transport_notice) before the conversation ended.

The agent miscalculated the credit amount as 13.50 instead of 15.00 because there were 10 remaining days between 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-12 (226.50 * 10 / 151 = 15.00), improperly copying the 9-day example from the policy.
The simulated customer ended the conversation prematurely with ###STOP### in the same turn they confirmed the extension, leaving the agent no opportunity to execute the write actions.
The agent miscalculated the credit amount as 13.50 (copying the example from the policy for 9 remaining days) instead of 12.00 for the 8 days between June 4 and June 12.

The simulated customer violated their instructions ('Accept whatever the agent says and do not ask for anything else') by making a new request to end service on June 12th instead of ending the conversation upon being refused.
The agent gave up after claiming it could not link property P-6038 to a taxpayer instead of looking up the property and taxpayer details to complete verification and grant the 20-day extension.
The policy specifies that requests for more than 30 days are declined and not reduced to 30, but the agent offered and executed a 30-day extension instead of declining the request.
The simulated customer violated their instructions by asking for a 30-day extension after 35 days was refused, instead of accepting the refusal and stopping.

The agent improperly solicited and processed a shortened request of 2 days after declining the customer's request for 6 days, violating the policy instruction to decline requests exceeding the limit rather than shortening them.

The policy instructs to decline when a check fails but does not prohibit offering alternative durations or processing a new valid request when the borrower accepts, whereas the grader strictly graded the initial request as refused with no write actions.
The simulated customer violated task instructions to accept the agent's decline calmly and stop, instead negotiating a 24-month term that prompted the agent to modify the account.

The simulated customer violated task instructions to switch to 45 days and accept whatever the agent decides by instead negotiating and requesting a 30-day extension when told 45 days was not allowed.
The simulated customer deviated from their scenario instructions by agreeing to a 30-day extension instead of accepting the refusal of 35 days and ending the conversation.
The simulated customer deviated from her scenario instructions by proposing June 11 instead of stopping the conversation after her June 30 request was refused.

The customer scenario instructed the user to accept the refusal after asking for an exception at least twice, but instead the customer pivoted and requested a different date (June 24, 2026), leading the agent to reschedule.
The agent mistakenly called create_refund twice, first with an incorrect amount of 1410 and then with 1380, leaving an extra duplicate refund in the database.
The agent miscalculated the number of days between 2026-06-01 and 2026-07-15 as 45 instead of 44, resulting in a refund amount of $975 instead of $950.
The agent correctly determined that an approval request was needed for a credit over $150.00, but failed to call the `create_approval_request` tool to actually open it.
The agent repeatedly asked for confirmation and explained what it would do instead of executing the required settle_claim and create_payment tool calls when all conditions were met.

The policy explicitly instructed the agent not to offer a different cancellation date on its own, but the agent suggested June 16th and processed the cancellation instead of refusing the customer's request.

The simulated customer included the stop token '###STOP###' in the same turn where they finally agreed to the reschedule and fee, ending the conversation prematurely before the agent had an opportunity to execute the tool calls.
The agent told the customer it would open a service manager review for warranty expiry, but failed to call the `create_manager_review` tool.
The agent processed a refund despite the membership having only 21 days remaining (from 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-10), violating the policy rule requiring at least 30 days left until the end date.
The simulated customer failed to change their mind to 1 payment before the agent completed anything as instructed by their scenario, prompting the agent to open a review request for 3 payments first.

The simulated customer violated task instructions by asking to switch back to premium economy instead of accepting the business refusal and ending the conversation, which led the agent to process an upgrade rather than concluding with a refusal.
The policy explicitly instructed not to offer a different date on its own, but the agent suggested alternative eligible date ranges and then processed a cancellation when it should have refused.
The agent asked for confirmation instead of directly issuing the credit as instructed by the policy, and thus took no write actions.
The customer appended ###STOP### immediately to their final confirmation ('Fine, whatever. Just do it.'), ending the conversation before the agent had an opportunity to execute the write actions.
The simulated customer was instructed to accept the agent's decision and end the conversation with ###STOP### when told the request could not be done, but instead requested 8 nights when prompted.
The agent failed to check the shipment's declared value ($78,500.00, exceeding $50,000.00) and placed the hold instead of routing it to terminal operations for review with reason 'high_value'.
The customer was instructed to accept the refusal of the inactive Old Mill Road stop and end the conversation, but instead asked to proceed with the Kingsley Park Entrance stop.
The agent offered to transfer the caller instead of executing the valid stop change or asking to proceed with the mandatory effective date of May 28th.
The agent asked the customer for confirmation instead of performing the required write actions (extending the agreement, setting the unit hold, and logging the extension) when all checks passed.
The agent incorrectly claimed that the new return date of May 27 conflicted with the May 28 reservation, failing to realize May 27 is strictly before May 28.
The agent told the customer it would open a service manager review for the 5-day extension due to repeat extensions, but failed to actually call the create_manager_review tool.

The policy states that if a customer asks for more than 7 days, the agent must decline the request rather than shortening it, but the agent proactively offered and executed a 7-day extension instead of refusing.
The agent failed to check the parcel record as explicitly required by the policy, missing that the parcel was scheduled for tax sale and therefore ineligible for an installment plan.
The simulated customer appended ###STOP### to end the conversation immediately upon giving confirmation, giving the agent no opportunity to execute the tool calls.

The agent was asked to evaluate the return segment SEG-640119 (which was already credited and should have been declined under R1), but instead proactively offered to credit and then credited the outbound segment SEG-640118.
The agent credited the flight despite more than 180 days having elapsed between the flight date (2025-11-16) and today (2026-05-20), violating Check 5 (Time limit).
The agent repeatedly asked for confirmation instead of executing the required stop change and seat adjustments directly as instructed by the policy when all conditions were satisfied.
The simulated customer was instructed to accept the refusal of Old Mill Rd and end the conversation, but instead asked to proceed with the Kingsley Park Entrance stop.
The simulated customer accepted the extension to May 27th but immediately appended '###STOP###', terminating the conversation before the agent had a turn to execute the extension tool calls.

The simulated customer was instructed to accept the agent's decision and end the conversation with ###STOP### when told it cannot be done, but instead requested a different number of nights (8 nights).
